ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether the large data-center order represents repeatable AI data-center demand or a one-time mega project; also whether Powell has manufacturing capacity and margin discipline to execute the backlog.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary-source confirmation of data-center backlog mix, repeat customer demand, order duration, cancellation terms, capacity expansion, and gross-margin sustainability.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Powell has the cleanest Serenity-style mapping in this chunk: AI data-center growth increases demand for medium-voltage switchgear, power control rooms, packaged electrical systems, and behind-the-meter or interconnection workarounds. The bottleneck is physical, capacity-constrained, order-book visible, and directly falsifiable through backlog, data-center order recurrence, margins, and manufacturing execution.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is commonly screened as a cyclical industrial electrical-equipment company rather than as a data-center power-delivery chokepoint. That creates a potentially overlooked second-order AI infrastructure signal.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether recent OSAT and HBM-related orders convert into sustained backlog, revenue, and gross margin without being a one-time capacity digestion cycle.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need filings and earnings-call evidence tying revenue growth to advanced packaging, HBM, OSAT, foundry, and substrate yield-control demand rather than a temporary equipment pull-forward.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: If advanced packaging and FC-BGA substrate constraints are yield-driven, inspection and metrology become natural second-order bottleneck beneficiaries. Camtek has a focused semiconductor inspection/metrology profile and a clear evidence path through OSAT demand, HBM/advanced packaging orders, backlog conversion, gross margin, and customer concentration.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is an Israeli Nasdaq-listed inspection/metrology specialist one layer away from GPUs, HBM, and substrate makers, so it can be missed by investors focused on obvious AI semiconductor leaders.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether the USD 4B capacity agreement is concentrated in one customer, what margin profile accompanies the capacity commitment, and whether orders are cancellable or tied to binding volume/price terms.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary-source details on capacity-agreement economics, customer concentration, cancellation rights, segment margin profile, data-center mix, and liquid-cooling versus conventional cooling contribution.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: AI rack density creates durable demand for facility cooling, CDUs, chillers, heat rejection, water-loop integration, and control systems. Modine ranks highly because a large capacity agreement, if durable and profitable, would indicate customer qualification and scarce capacity in data-center thermal management.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Historically viewed as a diversified thermal and industrial manufacturer rather than a pure AI data-center cooling supplier. The AI exposure may only recently have become visible through data-center cooling segmentation and customer commitments.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether recurring software, SaaS hosting, managed services, DERMS, grid analytics, and utility automation become a larger share of revenue and margin versus hardware deployment cycles.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary-source verification from filings, investor presentations, segment disclosures, and customer wins showing that software/managed-services growth is material and tied to utility grid complexity rather than ordinary meter replacement cycles.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Itron ranks highest because it is a cleaner Serenity-style second-order bottleneck candidate than the obvious AI cloud names: AI data-center load growth stresses utilities, forcing more grid-edge visibility, forecasting, DER control, metering intelligence, and operational resilience. The thesis is testable through recurring software mix, managed-services growth, utility backlog, margin progression, and DERMS/analytics disclosures.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It may screen as smart-meter hardware or utility equipment rather than as an operating layer for grid automation, utility data, resilience, and embedded critical-infrastructure workflows.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Advanced packaging revenue mix, PACE center activity, orders for Firefly, JetStep, inspection, metrology, or process-control tools from substrate makers, OSATs, and AI packaging customers.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary-source confirmation of AI advanced-packaging exposure, order concentration, substrate-maker adoption, and whether the relevant demand is incremental rather than cyclical semiconductor equipment recovery.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Onto is highly prioritized because the cached evidence frames advanced FC-BGA substrates as yield-constrained rather than merely capacity-constrained. If yield is the binding problem, inspection, metrology, lithography, and process-control software become required scaling tools for advanced packaging and substrate production.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is followed as a semiconductor equipment company, but the narrower substrate-yield and advanced-packaging process-control angle can be missed by investors focused on wafer-fab equipment or obvious GPU/HBM producers.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether MacDermid Alpha has meaningful revenue exposure to FC-BGA, ABF/IC substrates, AI/HPC substrate customers, substrate fabs, or leading OSAT/foundry advanced-packaging lines.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need segment-level evidence that MacDermid Alpha participates materially in IC substrate, ABF, mSAP, advanced packaging, or AI/HPC substrate processes; otherwise the thesis remains a broad electronics-chemicals inference.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Element Solutions is a strong shadow-beneficiary candidate because electronics process chemistry sits beneath advanced substrates and packaging, where yield and surface control matter. The opportunity is underfollowed because the AI exposure may be hidden inside MacDermid Alpha and specialty-chemicals segment labels.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It likely screens as specialty chemicals rather than as an AI advanced-packaging supplier. This messy industry label is exactly the kind of underfollowed discovery lane the Serenity framework is designed to catch.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Vicor wins sockets in next-generation GPU/accelerator platforms or rack-level 48V architectures, and whether design wins translate into volume revenue rather than prototype or evaluation visibility.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence of named or strongly inferable AI accelerator/rack design wins, revenue conversion, margin impact, and competitive positioning against alternative power architectures.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Vicor has a strong chokepoint setup because AI rack power density increases the value of compact, efficient, high-current power conversion. The research value is in determining whether 48V rack architectures and next-generation accelerator platforms create durable socket-level demand for Vicor modules.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is a component-level power-conversion company rather than an obvious AI data-center integrator, so AI exposure can be hidden inside qualification cycles, customer programs, and power-architecture transitions.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Data-center-specific revenue, backlog, pricing, product mix after the HDPE pipe/conduit business sale, and exposure to hyperscaler, colocation, electrical-contractor, or EPC data-center customers.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need company disclosures or channel evidence separating data-center demand from broader non-residential construction and confirming whether Atkore products are scarce enough to create pricing or margin resilience.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Atkore is a useful shadow-beneficiary candidate because data-center electrical buildouts require conduit, raceway, cable management, and related electrical infrastructure. It scores well on underfollowed discovery because the company may be obscured by non-residential construction cyclicality even if data-center electrical demand is strong.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It screens as a conventional electrical-products and construction supplier rather than as an AI power-delivery enabler; near-term cyclical weakness could hide data-center-specific product strength.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Contracted ARR versus actual revenue conversion, deployment schedule execution, counterparty concentration, GPU procurement financing, NVIDIA/Microsoft dependency, and whether claimed power access becomes energizable AI data-center capacity.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary evidence that AI contracts are durable, revenue-converting, adequately financed, and supported by real power/data-center execution rather than a temporary pivot narrative from crypto infrastructure.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: IREN ranks highly because the thesis sits at a real AI infrastructure constraint: secured power plus deployable data-center capacity. If customers value energizable AI capacity more than generic compute promises, former crypto-adjacent operators with power campuses can become bottleneck beneficiaries.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It has historically screened as Bitcoin mining or power-heavy digital infrastructure rather than as an AI cloud or AI data-center capacity platform, creating a messy-label discovery opportunity.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether liquid-cooling and data-center power products are becoming a material share of Enclosures or Electrical & Fastening Solutions growth, and whether customer qualification cycles create switching costs.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need segment disclosures showing material AI/data-center contribution, product-level growth in liquid cooling and power distribution, and evidence of qualification-based switching costs.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: nVent maps to both power and thermal density upgrades through electrical connection, enclosures, power distribution, and liquid-cooling-related data-center products. It has a plausible qualification and component-standardization angle, but may be less mispriced than smaller or messier names because the data-center infrastructure story is more visible.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Although large-cap, it is often categorized as electrical products and enclosures rather than an AI infrastructure component supplier. Its exposure sits below visible data-center integrators.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether reported ARR growth maps to real deployed GPU utilization, durable customer contracts, expansion with secured power, and non-transitory demand rather than temporary spot GPU scarcity.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence connecting ARR, utilization, customer quality, data-center capacity, GPU procurement, power access, and gross margin durability.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Nebius is prioritized as a possible public-market pure play on specialized AI cloud capacity scarcity, especially if enterprise and hyperscaler demand exceeds internal GPU capacity. It is less obviously underfollowed than small industrial suppliers but still may be misclassified due to its post-Yandex history.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Some investors may still categorize it as a post-Yandex international technology holding rather than as a scarce AI compute-capacity platform.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether leased megawatts are delivered on time, whether project financing is non-dilutive enough, and whether customer concentration around CoreWeave creates hidden counterparty risk.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need project-level delivery milestones, financing terms, customer contract durability, energization evidence, and unit economics for AI/HPC leases.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Applied Digital is a relevant AI/HPC data-center infrastructure candidate because the bottleneck may be deliverable power-to-compute capacity, not merely GPU procurement. Its score is capped by financing, execution, and customer-concentration risks.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It may be categorized as a legacy crypto-adjacent or speculative data-center developer rather than as a power-to-compute infrastructure candidate.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Arizona customer ramps, FCBGA/2.5D package revenue, substrate procurement constraints, and whether Amkor identifies substrates or materials as gating factors.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need segment-level or management-commentary evidence that AI advanced packaging is material and that substrates, materials, or process yield are true gating factors.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Amkor is a useful reference/customer-platform anchor for advanced packaging, FCBGA, 2.5D packaging, and substrate/material demand. It is less of a hidden chokepoint than upstream chemistry, substrate, or metrology suppliers, but its disclosures can help validate the broader advanced-packaging capacity and substrate constraint thesis.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Less underfollowed than chemistry/metrology names, but still less obvious than GPU, HBM, foundry, or hyperscaler leaders.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Determine whether KLIC tools are used in FC-BGA, 2.5D/3D advanced packaging, thermocompression bonding, high-density package assembly, or substrate-related process steps.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Company-specific AI advanced-packaging exposure is not yet proven. Need filings, investor presentations, order commentary, customer references, product mapping, and backlog evidence.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Hypothesis: if advanced packaging and substrate constraints are yield- and process-complexity driven, packaging-equipment suppliers can become second-order beneficiaries. KLIC is attractive for Layer 4 verification because the thesis is concrete and falsifiable: confirm whether its tools are used in thermocompression bonding, high-density package assembly, advanced substrate, 2.5D/3D, or AI accelerator package workflows.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Small-cap packaging-equipment names are less visible than GPUs, HBM, foundries, OSATs, and substrate leaders. KLIC may sit in an overlooked equipment lane if its tools touch AI package capacity or yield-control steps.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether contracted GPU capacity, customer concentration, GPU-backed financing, and utilization remain strong enough to support rapid capacity expansion without margin compression.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need ongoing verification of customer concentration, financing structure, utilization, capacity delivery, margin durability, and whether AI cloud scarcity persists as hyperscalers add internal capacity.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: CoreWeave remains important as the reference benchmark for specialized AI cloud capacity scarcity. It has high demand and purity scores, but lower underfollowed-discovery and mispricing scores because it is already widely recognized as a direct AI compute-capacity platform.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included as the benchmark capacity platform against which smaller, messier, or less obvious AI infrastructure names should be compared.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Contribution, growth rate and net retention of Tenable OT Security or customers buying Tenable One plus OT modules; utility, industrial and data-center customer evidence.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need proof that OT and critical-infrastructure security are material growth drivers and that data centers or utilities are specifically increasing attach rates, not merely broad cybersecurity budget growth.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Tenable is a plausible second-order beneficiary if AI infrastructure, utilities, and data-center expansion increase IT/OT convergence, asset discovery, vulnerability management, and compliance workflows. The thesis is attractive but less directly tied to a hard physical chokepoint than power, cooling, or packaging yield.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Often viewed as a mature vulnerability-management software company, while the OT-security and critical-infrastructure exposure may be buried inside broader exposure-management narratives.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Mix shift toward recurring ARR from Digi Remote Manager, Lighthouse/Opengear, SmartSense, and other managed services; customer evidence in data centers, utilities, industrials, transportation, and healthcare.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that recurring software and managed services are becoming material and that data-center, utility, or critical-infrastructure customers are incremental drivers rather than legacy industrial connectivity demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Digi has a strong underfollowed-discovery profile because secure remote connectivity, out-of-band management, edge device management, and industrial IoT can become operational necessities as infrastructure becomes more distributed and mission-critical. However, the AI data-center linkage needs more proof than the physical power/cooling names.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is usually categorized as industrial IoT or connectivity hardware rather than cybersecurity or AI infrastructure operations software.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Actual AI cloud ARR, number and type of GPUs deployed, customer contracts, conversion cost per MW, suitability of existing sites for high-density AI loads, and whether colocation demand is binding or merely exploratory.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need hard evidence of contracted AI revenue, deployed GPUs, power capacity available for AI, customer quality, capex per MW, cooling suitability, and economics versus pure Bitcoin mining.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Hypothesis: powered sites, grid access, and fast-to-convert digital infrastructure can become bottlenecks if AI colocation and specialized AI cloud demand remain strong. BTDR has potentially high mispricing potential because it may be screened as a Bitcoin-mining company rather than an AI infrastructure conversion candidate.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: The messy industry label creates a discovery opportunity and a risk. Generalist AI investors may miss AI colocation optionality, while crypto-focused investors may overweight Bitcoin-mining economics.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Quantify data-center order growth, backlog duration, pricing power, and whether supply constraints are in switchgear, transformers, breakers, busway, or services.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need current segment-level data-center exposure, backlog duration, pricing, margin contribution, and specific product bottleneck disclosure.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Fact/inference blend: AI data-center buildout requires electrical distribution, switchgear, transformers, breakers, busway, and services. ETN is a high-quality reference leader for checking whether the power-delivery bottleneck is real and whether smaller candidates have comparable backlog, pricing, and capacity signals.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed. It is included as a benchmark to discipline smaller-name research and prevent confusing weak shadow exposure with true bottleneck economics.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Attach rate of cybersecurity software/licensing to industrial networking deployments, contribution from virtual firewall and OT security products, and exposure to utilities, data centers, transit and process automation.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need filings or investor materials quantifying cybersecurity/software contribution, vertical mix, recurring revenue, and whether data-center or utility customers are driving incremental demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Belden fits the proxy-beneficiary framework: industrial networks, cables, secure OT networking, segmentation, firewalls, and operational visibility may matter more as utilities, factories, transit systems, and data centers become more connected. The hidden signal is plausible but needs evidence of software/security attach and AI-infrastructure relevance.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Belden is commonly viewed as a cables/connectivity or industrial networking company rather than as an OT security and data-infrastructure chokepoint.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether TDK mentions powder availability, ceramic slurry/formulation constraints, or thin-layer MLCC material bottlenecks in earnings calls or technical materials.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that AI-server MLCC demand is materially affecting TDK mix, margins, lead times, or supplier constraints, and that upstream powder scarcity is visible in company commentary.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: TDK is useful as a reference leader for the AI-server MLCC and upstream dielectric-powder chain. It can help verify whether MLCC count, thin-layer capacity, material quality, and powder availability are becoming bottlenecks. It ranks lower as a candidate because it is less underfollowed and less pure as a public-market expression of the upstream powder thesis.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included mainly as a reference verifier for the MLCC and barium titanate dielectric-powder bottleneck thesis.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Post-acquisition disclosures that separate CyberArk/identity ARR, customer overlap, regulated-industry traction, and integration into Palo Alto security operations products.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that AI infrastructure and critical-infrastructure operations create incremental cybersecurity attach rates beyond the company’s already broad platform growth narrative.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Palo Alto Networks is retained only as a cybersecurity platform reference for AI-era cloud, identity, security operations, and critical-infrastructure cybersecurity. It is not the main alpha-hunt candidate because it is too visible and broad to be a clean underfollowed chokepoint.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included only as a reference anchor so smaller OT, identity, automation, and infrastructure-management vendors are not evaluated in isolation.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Precision Devices revenue mix, MLCC capacity/utilization, high-reliability capacitor backlog, end-market exposure to data-center power, networking, aerospace, or defense compute.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need proof that KN supplies relevant MLCC or specialty capacitor products into AI-server, accelerator-board, networking, or data-center power applications.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Hypothesis: AI servers and accelerator boards may increase demand for high-reliability MLCCs and specialty ceramic capacitors. KN is worth verification because capacitor exposure may be hidden inside Precision Devices rather than obvious from company-level screens.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Knowles is usually framed around precision devices, audio, RF, and specialty components, not as a possible AI-server capacitor or MLCC supply-chain node.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify OTC tradability/liquidity for NPNHF and determine whether MLCC-related barium compounds or BaTiO3 products are material to revenue or margins.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need product-level confirmation, customer evidence, MLCC-related revenue materiality, particle-size/spec quality, capacity, margins, and practical public-market access.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Speculative hypothesis: if AI-server MLCC demand tightens high-purity barium compounds or barium titanate materials, a small Japanese specialty-chemical supplier could be a hidden upstream beneficiary. The candidate deserves only cautious follow-up because investability, liquidity, and revenue materiality are unresolved.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: The company is small, Japanese, chemically diversified, and not obviously labeled as an AI infrastructure supplier. Any MLCC input exposure may be buried inside functional products.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether AI/cloud complexity is translating into net retention, usage-based growth, automation adoption, and expansion with large infrastructure-heavy customers.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that AI/cloud complexity is specifically driving incremental usage, retention, automation adoption, large-customer expansion, or infrastructure-heavy customer wins.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Hypothesis: AI/cloud infrastructure complexity may increase demand for operational resilience, incident response, automation, and always-on infrastructure workflows. PD has a clean SaaS measurement path, but its link to physical AI infrastructure bottlenecks is indirect.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Often screened as a slower-growth SaaS incident-management company rather than as a resilience and automation layer for increasingly complex AI/cloud operations.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether KYOCERA AVX supplies high-capacitance or high-reliability MLCCs into AI accelerator boards, server power systems, networking equipment, or hyperscaler-qualified supply chains.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need segment/product-level evidence linking KYOCERA AVX capacitors to AI servers, accelerator boards, networking systems, or hyperscaler-qualified supply chains.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Hypothesis: KYOCERA AVX could have hidden exposure to high-reliability MLCCs and specialty capacitors used in server power, networking, RF/microwave, aerospace, industrial, and mission-critical electronics. However, Kyocera is diversified, reducing public-market purity.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: KYOCERA AVX is embedded inside a larger Japanese conglomerate, so any AI-server MLCC exposure may be diluted and not highlighted in mainstream AI infrastructure coverage.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Materion sells commercial BaTiO3 powder into electronic ceramics or MLCC supply chains, whether particle-size specs reach high-end MLCC requirements, and whether customers include capacitor makers.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need confirmation that Materion has relevant BaTiO3 products, high-end MLCC-grade specifications, customer relationships with capacitor makers, and material revenue exposure.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Weak hypothesis: US specialty-material suppliers with relevant ceramic or barium titanate capabilities could benefit if high-end MLCC dielectric-powder supply tightens. MTRN is worth a low-priority check, but current AI-server linkage is weak.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Materion is usually classified as a broad advanced-materials company, so any capacitor-ceramics exposure may be buried inside a larger materials portfolio.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Cabot still owns any barium titanate ceramics business after past strategic reviews, or whether those assets were sold, shut down, or moved into another private supplier.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Current evidence is too stale. Need confirmation of ownership, product existence, commercial BaTiO3 capability, MLCC customer exposure, and revenue materiality.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Speculation only: CBT remains in the ranked chunk because a stale possibility of barium titanate or ceramic-material exposure can be quickly falsified. It should not advance without current evidence that the relevant business exists and is material.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Cabot is followed mainly for carbon black, battery materials, and specialty chemicals, not MLCC dielectric powders. That may reflect a real coverage gap, but more likely reflects lack of current relevant exposure.

summary: Split Layer 3 ranking merged from candidate chunks.
